summary.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊 and commonly means “side” or “edge,” including a margin or border. Analyses of 邊’s early components differ over which parts carry meaning and sound.

formation.text: 邊’s early construction is disputed. One analysis assigns movement meaning to 辵 and a sound role to 𦤝; another assigns “beside” to 方 and proposes sound roles for 自 and 丙. 边 is the simplified form of 邊.

components.text: One analysis of 邊 assigns 辵 a movement meaning. Its conventional left-side form is 辶; this proposed role in 邊 is not established for 边.
A Han-era dictionary analysis identifies 𦤝 as 邊’s sound element. Its graphic relationship to 臱 remains unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: Zhengzhang’s reconstruction compares 臱 *men with 邊 *mpeːn, but the evidence does not establish that 𦤝 is 臱. This pair therefore cannot validate 𦤝’s proposed sound role.

sound.text: The reported Mandarin readings are 𦤝 mián and 邊 biān. This modern comparison does not establish the proposed ancient sound role.
sound.system: Mandarin: CNS11643 reading for 𦤝 and Modern Standard Mandarin for 邊

components.text: One analysis of the bronze form assigns 方 the meaning “beside”; a competing analysis assigns meaning to 辵.
Some analyses propose that 自 supplies sound in early 邊. Its Mandarin reading zì differs from 邊 biān and does not establish that historical role.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship for 自 in 邊.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are 自 zì and 邊 biān; they differ and do not establish an ancient sound match.

components.text: Some analyses propose that 丙 supplies sound in early 邊. Its Mandarin reading bǐng differs from 邊 biān and does not establish that historical role.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship for 丙 in 邊.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are 丙 bǐng and 邊 biān; they differ and do not establish an ancient sound match.

components.text: 边 is simplified from 邊 and retains 辶, the conventional left-side form of 辵. This form correspondence does not establish the disputed movement meaning for 辶 in 边.

history.text: Oracle-script-style, bronze-script-style, and Chu silk-script-style redraws represent 邊 in different script traditions. They do not establish a sequence of graphic changes.
边 was officially adopted as the simplified form of 邊 in 1956. The cited account does not document the graphic steps.

uncertainties.text: Early analyses disagree: one assigns movement meaning to 辵 and sound to 𦤝; others assign “beside” to 方 and propose sound roles for 自 and 丙. The accounts do not resolve which analysis best explains the early graph.
One account calls 臱 the original graph, but whether it directly precedes 邊 or the earliest form was already 邊 remains unresolved.

Zhengzhang reconstructions compare 臱 *men with 邊 *mpeːn, and the Han-era dictionary assigns a sound role to 𦤝. Whether 𦤝 and 臱 are graphically related remains unresolved, so that comparison cannot establish 𦤝’s sound role. Proposed sound roles for 自 and 丙 also lack comparable ancient readings for those elements in 邊.

The selected redraws do not establish a graphic sequence: the oracle- and bronze-style examples are not tied to specific dated artifacts, and the cited silk manuscript image is not examined in the file description.

senses.text: One analysis proposes “beside” as an original sense of 邊; its earliest attestation and date remain unresolved.
A use of 邊 meaning “frontier region” is reported in a bronze inscription, but its date and place in the word’s history remain unresolved.
边 and 邊 commonly mean a side or edge, including a margin or border. Their first occurrence and any continuous development from “beside” remain unresolved.

senses.gloss: while, in the paired construction 邊…邊…
senses.text: 邊 is also used in the paired construction 邊…邊… to mean “while.” Its chronology and development from spatial meanings remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish securely dated first occurrences for each sense or a continuous development from “beside” through “frontier” or “edge” to the paired “while” construction.

overview.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊 and commonly means “side” or “edge.” The traditional graph’s early components have competing analyses of their meaning and sound roles.

components.text: In 邊, 辶 is the left-side form of 辵; one disputed analysis assigns it movement meaning. That role is not established for 边.
The comparison of 臱 *men with 邊 *mpeːn does not establish that 𦤝 is graphically related to 臱 or validate its proposed sound role.
One analysis assigns 方 the meaning “beside”; another assigns a meaning role to 辵.
Some analyses propose 自 as a sound element in 邊, but modern readings 自 zì and 邊 biān do not establish that ancient role.
Some analyses propose 丙 as a sound element in 邊, but modern readings 丙 bǐng and 邊 biān do not establish that ancient role.

relationships.text: One analysis of 邊 treats 辶, the left-side form of 辵, as contributing movement meaning; analyses of the early graph differ.
The Han-era account identifies 𦤝 as the sound element of 邊, while other analyses propose sound roles for different parts of the early graph.
One analysis of the bronze form assigns 方 the meaning “beside,” differing from the movement-based account of 辵.
Some analyses propose that 自 marks sound in early 邊, but comparable ancient readings for 自 in this character are not supplied.
Some analyses propose that 丙 marks sound in early 邊, but comparable ancient readings for 丙 in this character are not supplied.
